title: Associate Director, HEOR & Market Access, EU West
description:
Mavericks Wanted

When was the last time you achieved the impossible? If that thought feels overwhelming, you might want to pause here, but if it sparks excitement...read on

In 2015, we pioneered a “moneyball for biotech” approach, pooling projects and promising early-stage research from academia together under one financial umbrella to reduce risk and unleash innovation. This model allows science and small teams of experts to lead the way. We build bridges to groundbreaking advancements in rare disease, and develop life-changing medicines for patients with unmet needs as fast as humanly possible.

Together we define white space, push boundaries, and empower people to solve problems. If you're someone who defies convention, join us and work alongside some of the most respected minds in the industry. Together, we'll ask "why not?" and help reengineer the future of biopharma. At BridgeBio, we value curiosity and experimentation—including the ethical & thoughtful use of AI to improve clarity, speed, and quality of work.

What You’ll Do

You will report to the Senior Director, Head of Market Access, EU West Region and work closely with Medical affairs, Market Access, Commercial locally and globally, to support BridgeBio’s mission of delivering transformative medicines to patients with genetic rare diseases.

You will own the value demonstration strategy for our products across the region, and translate it into effective patient access: design each product's evidence generation plan, drive it through to delivery, and align it with pricing and access strategy, starting in France, then extending to the other countries of the EU West region

Your main responsibilities include:

Evidence generation

  • Design and lead natural history studies, cohorts, registries, and analyses of medico-administrative databases (SNDS, BNDMR/ BaMaRa, rare disease network registries)
  • Lead indirect comparisons in the context of single-arm trials and very small patient populations
  • Develop health economic models (cost-effectiveness, budget impact) for France, then for other markets in the region
  • Design real-world data collection frameworks (PUT-RD / data collection protocols) that can be reused for reassessment and in other countries
  • Define the scientific publication and communication plan

Study management

  • Draft specifications, run tenders, and select vendors
  • Convene and lead external scientific advisory committees
  • Secure all required approvals (health data access, ethics committees, regulatory compliance)
  • Manage the administrative, contractual, and budgetary aspects of studies
  • Review and validate all deliverables (protocols, analysis plans, study reports, publications)

Value communication and internal expertise

  • Translate study results into actionable clinical and economic arguments
  • Drive scientific dissemination (congresses, publications)
  • Serve as the internal reference point on epidemiology, health economics, and health data matters
  • Build and maintain a network of research agencies, academics, and institutions

Value and access strategy

  • Define and own the value demonstration strategy for each product across the region
  • Build economic value propositions and value dossiers and ensure their local adaptation
  • Contribute to pricing strategy and preparation for CEPS negotiations (e.g., positive externalities, budget impact)
  • Coordinate and build the economic modelling and CEESP dossier (early scientific advice, modelling, CEESP submission, technical exchange, etc.)
  • Contribute the health-economic and RWE content of early access dossiers and submissions to the Transparency Committee, in coordination with the Market Access Director, with progressively increasing ownership of Benelux dossiers
  • Anticipate assessors' objections and build responses ahead of submission

French rare disease ecosystem

  • Build working relationships with rare disease networks, reference and competence centres, patient associations, and learned societies
  • Negotiate collaborations with existing registries and cohorts
  • Contribute to documenting the patient journey and disease burden

Function leadership and development

  • Own and arbitrate the region's HEOR and RWE budget
  • Structure the function (methods, quality standards, vendor panel, review processes)
  • Recruit and manage future team members
  • Represent the region to global HEOR and Market Access teams

The above list of tasks is not exhaustive.

Where You’ll Work

  • This is a France-based role
  • Travel within France, a priority country, is expected, as is travel to our international office in Zug, Switzerland, for team alignment and engagement.
  • Travel to other countries in the EU West region may also be required. Local team meetings and the designated office location in France are in the Paris area.

Who You Are

  • 7–10 years of experience in HEOR, real-world evidence (RWE), or market access within industry, biotech, or specialized consulting
  • Direct, hands-on experience completing French market access dossiers, including submissions to the Transparency Committee, early access applications, and CEESP assessments
  • Strong knowledge of observational studies, medico-administrative databases, health economic modeling, and indirect comparisons
  • Proven experience managing vendors and budgets
  • Ability to influence without direct authority and collaborate with global, multidisciplinary teams
  • A background in pharmacy, medicine, epidemiology, health economics, or biostatistics, with a master’s or doctoral degree
  • Fluency in French and professional proficiency in English

Strongly preferred

  • Experienced in rare or ultra-rare diseases
  • Experienced defending a surrogate endpoint or biomarker
  • Knowledge of French rare disease networks
  • Exposure to Belgian, Dutch, or Central and Eastern European systems
  • Initial people management experience
  • Experience in biotech or a fast-growing organization

Expected attributes

  • Quickly operate independently, with a strong sense of ownership
  • Ability to prioritize across multiple geographies
  • Critical thinking and methodological rigor
  • Compelling communication in both French and English
  • Directness and clarity in all exchanges

As a global company, our comprehensive benefits may vary based on location. We have high expectations for our team members. We make sure those working hard for patients are rewarded and cared for in return.

For BridgeBio Full-Time U.S Based Roles:

Financial & Rewards

  • Market-leading compensation
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP)
  • Pre-tax commuter benefits (transit and parking)
  • Referral bonus for hired candidates
  • Subsidized lunch and parking on in-office days

Health & Well-Being

  • 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision premiums for you and your dependents
  • Health Savings Account (HSA) with annual employer contributions, plus Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
  • Fertility & family-forming benefits
  • Expanded mental health support (therapy and coaching resources)
  • Hybrid work model with flexibility
  • Flexible, “take-what-you-need” paid time off and company-paid holidays
  • Comprehensive paid medical and parental leave to care for yourself and your family

Skill Development & Career Paths:

  • People are part of our growth and success story - from discovery to active drug trials and FDA pipelines, there are endless opportunities for skill development and internal mobility
  • We provide career pathing through regular feedback, continuous education and professional development programs via LinkedIn Learning, LifeLabs, & BetterUp Coaching
  • We celebrate strong performance with financial rewards, peer-to-peer recognition, and growth opportunities

By applying, you acknowledge that BridgeBio will process your personal information as described in our Global Candidate Privacy Notice. Questions or requests: dataprivacy@bridgebio.com

title: Model Developer
description:
Within Insurance Technology, we are looking for a Model Developer who will take the lead in programming future-proof calculation tools. Do you enjoy analyzing complex code and intricate calculations? And are you able to translate your findings into pragmatic, actionable advice? If so, we would love to meet you and welcome you to the Insurance Technology team within the Expert Center Services of NN Life & Pensions.

What you are going to do

The Insurance Technology team provides specialist expertise to high-profile projects and transformation initiatives. We work in multidisciplinary teams and are responsible for ensuring the actuarial accuracy of calculations, both within strategic programs and across our calculation applications and IT systems. In doing so, we safeguard the interests of our customers and Nationale-Nederlanden.

To ensure that our testing tools and information systems remain future-proof, you will take the lead in modernizing and developing our software solutions. In addition, you will advise stakeholders across the value chain on quantitative issues.

In this role, you will:

  • Future-proof actuarial models by translating them into Python code
  • Provide subject-matter expertise to strategic projects and migration programs
  • Develop testing software to safeguard the actuarial accuracy of calculation engines and IT systems

What we offer you
NN invests in an inclusive, inspiring work environment and in skills and competences for the future. We match this with employee benefits that are in line with what is needed today and in the future. This way, we offer our employees the opportunity to get the best out of themselves. We offer you:

  • Salary between €3,891 and €5,188 based on a 36-hour work week, depending on your knowledge and experience
  • 13th month and holiday allowance are paid with your monthly salary
  • 27 vacation days for a 5-day working week and three Diversity Days
  • A modern pension administered by BeFrank
  • Plenty of training and learning opportunities
  • NS Business Card 2nd class, which gives you unlimited travel, also privately
    Do you prefer to travel with your own transport? Then you can declare the kilometers travelled
  • Allowances for setting up your home office and for internet use

Who you are

You have a strong quantitative background, enjoy intellectual challenges, and have an affinity for IT. You can quickly find your way through mathematical models and are able to translate complex code into clear and understandable language. You are positive, enjoy sharing ideas, and are open to different perspectives, making you a valued and collaborative colleague.

In addition, you have:

  • A Master's degree or equivalent academic working and thinking level
  • Experience programming in Python; knowledge of VBA and/or object-oriented languages such as C# or Java is a plus
  • Knowledge of statistical methods and the ability to explain complex analyses clearly to stakeholders
  • A curious, pragmatic mindset and a strong drive to get things done
  • C2-level proficiency in Dutch

Who you will work with

The Insurance Technology team is part of the Expert Center Services within NN Life & Pensions. Together with 13 experienced Modelers, Analysts, Actuaries, and Testing Experts, we serve as the actuarial center of expertise within the Services domain.

Working in multidisciplinary teams, we collaborate closely with colleagues from IT, Legal, Finance, and Risk Management.

We work in a hybrid environment with flexible working hours. Dedicated office days enable us to meet and collaborate in person, while the right tools and facilities allow us to stay connected and work effectively from home.

Any questions?

Any questions about the process can be directed to Hilde Diemel: Talent Acquisition Specialist via hilde.diemel@nn-group.com.

title: Director of Sustainability and Environment (APAC)
description:
Company Overview

STACK Infrastructure builds, owns, and operates hyperscale and colocation data centers that power the world’s most ambitious technology companies. With a rapidly expanding footprint across APAC, STACK combines deep development expertise, flexible capital, and operational discipline to deliver critical digital infrastructure at scale.

Our clients include the largest hyperscale cloud platforms. We are building a regional platform defined by speed of delivery, power reliability, and long-term partnership — and we are assembling the team to lead that effort.

About STACK

STACK INFRASTRUCTURE (STACK) is an award-winning industry leader in building, owning, and operating highly efficient, cost-effective wholesale, colocation, and cloud data centers. We provide digital infrastructure that enables the world’s most innovative companies to scale, with facilities that meet or exceed the highest industry standards for availability, security, connectivity, and physical resilience.

As a well-established data center business across APAC, the Americas, and Europe, STACK has successfully built several data centers in Melbourne and continues to expand its project portfolio with the goal of becoming a market leader in the hyperscale data center market.

STACK offers the scale and geographic reach that rapidly growing hyperscale and enterprise companies need. The world runs on data, Data runs on STACK.


About the role

The Director, Sustainability and Environment APAC owns the sustainability and environmental strategy for STACK developments through design, consent, construction readiness and operations. The role also leads the integrated sustainability and building-services ESD workstreams. It ensures that authority requirements, environmental obligations, energy-performance objectives and sustainability commitments are understood early, translated into design requirements and closed through clear, defensible submissions and reporting. Reporting to the Senior Vice President Engineering APAC, the role directs environmental, acoustic, sustainability and building-services ESD consultants; coordinates multidisciplinary technical reports, energy models and sustainability-rating submissions; and provides practical advice to Development, Engineering, Design Management, Delivery and Operations teams.


Key responsibilities

  • Define the environmental approval pathway for new sites, campus expansions and major design changes

  • Lead environmental due diligence for prospective sites and identify approval risks, fatal flaws, mitigation measures and information needed before acquisition or design commitment

  • Develop project design documents for local development applications, Victorian planning approvals, New South Wales State Significant Development Applications and other state or Commonwealth pathways where applicable

  • Act as STACK's principal design-side interface with EPA Victoria, NSW EPA, local councils, state planning departments and other referral authorities

  • Set the scope, evidence standard and review process for environmental impact assessments, planning reports, sustainability management plans, acoustic assessments, General Environmental Duty and supporting technical studies

  • Lead responses to council, state and regulator comments on development technical submissions

  • Direct and critically review specialist studies covering operational and construction acoustics, air quality and emissions, contaminated land, surface water and groundwater, waste, ecology and biodiversity, cultural heritage, landscape and visual impact, climate risk and other project-specific matters

  • Lead the integrated project sustainability and building-services ESD strategy from site selection and concept design through construction, commissioning and operational handover

  • Set energy-performance objectives and direct energy modelling across design stages

  • Establish and manage the sustainability-rating and certification strategy, including target setting, consultant coordination, evidence registers, submissions, assessor or authority comments and achievement tracking


About you

  • A relevant tertiary qualification in environmental science, environmental engineering, planning, sustainability, law or a related discipline

  • At least 10 years of progressive experience in environmental and sustainable design

  • Substantial recent experience within a multidisciplinary or specialist environmental consultancy team, directing approvals and technical assessment work for major developments or infrastructure, or Client-side experience following a senior consulting career, or evidence of working as an extension of a developer or asset owner team

  • Approvals experience for data centres, power generation, energy infrastructure, logistics, industrial facilities or other developments with material noise, air quality, water and community interfaces

  • Experience across both development approval and post-consent compliance, including construction environmental management and operational monitoring commitments

  • Experience with recognised Australian or international sustainability-rating frameworks and sustainability performance reporting for data centres, major infrastructure, industrial facilities or other energy-intensive assets

  • Demonstrated experience with Victorian and New South Wales approval systems, including direct engagement with EPA, councils and state planning authorities

  • Strong working knowledge of environmental legislation, the General Environmental Duty, planning permit and development consent processes, regulator expectations and the management of approval conditions

  • Proven ability to direct and review multidisciplinary technical reports, including environmental impact assessments, acoustics, sustainability management plans, building-services ESD strategies, energy models, sustainability-rating submissions and performance reports

  • Strong written communication, negotiation and presentation skills, with the judgement to brief executives and resolve complex issues with authorities and technical specialists
